note.text: A context clue is evidence from surrounding language. A definition, contrast, example or consequence can help explain an unfamiliar word. The clue supports a meaning; it does not justify any guess that sounds interesting. A collocation is a conventional word combination, such as make a decision or heavy rain. A synonym may fit a definition yet sound unnatural with a particular partner. Check grammar and meaning together, and use a dictionary when the context is insufficient.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to infer a supported word meaning from context and choose a natural word combination. Builds on: word classes and sentence meaning. Leads to: careful reading of trade passages and precise writing.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: A context clue is evidence from surrounding language. A definition, contrast, example or consequence can help explain an unfamiliar word. The clue supports a meaning; it does not justify any guess that sounds interesting. A collocation is a conventional word combination, such as make a decision or heavy rain. A synonym may fit a definition yet sound unnatural with a particular partner. Check grammar and meaning together, and use a dictionary when the context is insufficient.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original example: The path was slippery, so Bih moved carefully to avoid falling. The consequence supports a surface on which slipping is easy. A club can make a decision and do homework, but exchanging make and do mechanically creates unnatural combinations. Heavy rain is ordinary wording; strong rain is not the neutral model taught here.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Locate the exact clue and explain how it supports your interpretation. Separate a contextual inference from a fact not given. When choosing a collocation, consider the whole phrase rather than the isolated meaning of one word.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: A definition clue requires no explanatory wording. Correction: The nearby explanation supplies the meaning.
A contrast always means the words are synonyms. Correction: Opposition can distinguish the relevant properties.
Any synonym can replace any word in a collocation naturally. Correction: Conventional combinations constrain the choice.
A guess with no textual clue is automatically proven. Correction: An inference must connect to evidence in the passage.
